titel: The Music Industry Has Changed—Here's How to Win With A&R Executive Jacob Fain [Chainsmokers, Russ, Bailey Zimmerman]

faehigkeiten.grund: Dynamik weder belegt noch ausgeschlossen (Abruf laeuft ueber den Werbedienst podtrac.com) - zu wenig fuer ein Urteil, aber nicht nichts

einzeiler: Music executive Jacob Fain on A&R, authenticity, and artist development.
kurzfassung: Music executive Jacob Fain discusses his two decades in A&R and publishing, sharing insights on how artist signing criteria have shifted from pure data to cultural impact and authenticity. He explains the importance of resilience, teamwork, and a strong work ethic through examples like Russ and Bailey Zimmerman. Additionally, Fain recommends key books and documentaries for aspiring music industry professionals.
stichpunkte: Jacob Fain brings over two decades of experience across major and independent labels and music publishing.
The criteria for signing artists has shifted away from purely mathematical research back toward culture, music, and the artist's unique spark.
Authenticity is one of the most important currencies in the music business because fans can easily detect insincerity.
Persistence is a critical differentiator, highlighted by artists like Russ who spent years building an audience before achieving massive success.
An artist's team, such as management, can make or break their career and requires careful alignment.
Common pitfalls holding artists back include a lack of work ethic and the false assumption that success will come easily.
While artists have more power and autonomy than ever, partnering with a label eventually becomes necessary to scale globally.
Recommended reading and viewing for industry aspirants include works by Bill Walsh, Ed Catmull, and Priyanka Parker.

kapitel.titel: The Importance of Teams and Work Ethic
The Role of Record Labels Today

clips.hook: You can't mathematically figure out A&R
clips.text: Jacob Fain argues that relying solely on data analytics is insufficient for A&R, emphasizing that musical intuition and cultural relevance remain essential for success.

clips.hook: If I gave up after 9 years, no one would fault me
clips.text: Persistence is key in the music industry, as evidenced by an artist who finally achieved sold-out shows after nine years of struggling to gain traction.

clips.hook: Data can't tell you if an artist has the X factor
clips.text: When evaluating talent, Fain prioritizes identifying unique star power and artists who offer a fresh, provocative perspective that resonates with the public.

clips.hook: If you're not a consummate learner, you're holding yourself back
clips.text: Continuous learning and intellectual curiosity are vital for professional growth, which is why Fain mandates a book and movie club for his team.

clips.hook: Social media can be so destructive for artists
clips.text: Artists often struggle with feelings of inadequacy compared to their peers, but Fain reminds them that most musicians are viewed with envy by those just starting out.
